name: h1-block-held-signal
rationale: Second point on the one axis that produced the largest measured improvement in this pipeline's history, chosen specifically to land on the promotable side of the trade-count floor. Yesterday's `h6-block-held-signal` quantised the composite onto UTC-aligned 6-hour blocks and cut the number of distinct composite values from 15,462 to 57 (271x); at 500,000 JPY that moved Sharpe from -29.692 to -5.198 and return from -16.49% to -3.09% on 34 real trades — the largest single-variant gain this pipeline has ever recorded — but at the 50,000 JPY promotion capital it degenerated to exactly 1 trade and was refused on `MIN_TRADE_COUNT_RATIO` alone, as were the other two variants that day. The mechanism is therefore established and the open question is purely one of dose: 1-hour blocks give 336 blocks over the 14-day holdout instead of 56, a 60x slowdown of the signal clock rather than 360x, which is the largest slowdown that still plausibly clears the floor's 38-trade requirement against today's 76-trade baseline. arXiv:2602.11708 predicts H1 should be WORSE than H6 (Sharpe 1.54 at 847 trades/month vs 2.41 at 142), so this is a genuine test rather than a confirmation: if shirube's own H1 lands between the baseline and yesterday's H6 the frequency/Sharpe relationship is monotonic over three points and can be fitted; if H1 matches H6 the effect saturates early and the cheapest dose is the right one. Either answer is worth more than another single sample, and unlike H6 this one can actually be promoted. Note the mechanism is deliberately distinct from `rebalance-spacing-15m` (rejected), which throttled how often the engine may ACT while leaving the signal free to whipsaw: here the rebalance cadence, threshold, zone mapping and every indicator period stay byte-identical and only the composite is held, so drift-correcting trades against a held target still occur every candle.
code_change_summary: Quantise the composite onto fixed UTC-aligned blocks: recompute it only when a new block starts, and hold the previous value for the rest of the block. This is the same mechanism yesterday's `h6-block-held-signal` implemented at 21600 seconds; that worktree was deleted with the rejected variant, so it must be re-implemented here at 3600. Three coupled changes, NONE of which touch TradingEngine::compute_btc_target. (1) src/config.rs: add `pub signal_block_secs: u64` to TradingConfig with `#[serde(default = "default_signal_block_secs")]` returning 0, where 0 means 'no blocking — recompute every bar', i.e. exactly today's behaviour. Set it to 0 in TradingConfig::default(). Extend TradingConfig::validate() to reject a value that is neither 0 nor a positive multiple of 60 (a block shorter than one bar is meaningless at BASE_RESOLUTION = 60), with a Japanese error message matching the surrounding style. Add a unit test that a config JSON lacking the field deserialises to 0. (2) Add one pure helper, `pub(crate) fn block_start(ts: chrono::DateTime<chrono::Utc>, block_secs: u64) -> Option<i64>` on TradingEngine, returning None when block_secs == 0 and otherwise `Some(ts.timestamp().div_euclid(block_secs as i64))` — the index of the UTC-aligned block the timestamp falls in. Document the formula, the alignment guarantee (blocks start at UTC midnight for any block_secs that divides 86400, which 3600 does), and a NOTE citing this hypothesis and arXiv:2602.11708. (3) Apply it at BOTH sites that turn a composite into an allocation target. In src/backtest/simulator.rs::run, carry a `last_block: Option<i64>` and a `held_composite: Option<f64>` alongside the existing `sticky_target` and `last_rebalance_at` state; on each candle compute the candle's block index from `candle.open_time`, and only call compute_btc_target when the block index differs from `last_block` (or when signal_block_secs is 0), storing the result in `held_composite`; on every other candle reuse `held_composite` unchanged. Feed `held_composite` into the existing `* range_max` + apply_zone + threshold + allocation_delta_to_order path with no other modification, so drift-correcting rebalances against a HELD target still happen every candle exactly as they do today. In src/trading/engine.rs::handle_indicator, carry the same two pieces of state on TradingEngine and apply the identical rule, using the IndicatorOutput's `calculated_at` as the timestamp; when the composite is held, skip the compute_btc_target call and reuse the held value to build the target (do not change the sticky_target semantics — a held composite still updates sticky_target exactly as a freshly computed one would, and a None from compute_btc_target at a block boundary must leave the held value untouched rather than clearing it). Add unit tests covering: block_secs = 0 returns None from block_start; two timestamps 5 minutes apart inside one 1-hour block share a block index; timestamps straddling an hour boundary do not; 3600-second blocks align to the top of each UTC hour. In your report, state how many distinct composite values the run produced versus the number of evaluated candles (expect roughly 336 blocks over the 14-day holdout against ~15,400 candles), the realised composite band (min/max/sd) for both the blocked and unblocked formulas over the identical evaluated candles, how many trades fired on the first evaluated candle of a block versus mid-block as genuine drift corrections, and `orders_below_min` at all three capitals.
constraints: MUST NOT change TradingEngine::compute_btc_target's signature (its parameter list or return type) or its body — this hypothesis changes only HOW OFTEN that function is consulted, so the composite formula is held fixed and the measured effect is attributable to the sampling change alone.

MUST apply the blocking at BOTH call sites (the live site in src/trading/engine.rs::handle_indicator and the backtest site in src/backtest/simulator.rs::run), so the backtest cannot measure a strategy the live engine would not run. NOTE the known live/backtest cadence divergence carried in recent reports: SignalEngine::run republishes every 250 ms live while the backtest evaluates once per 60 s bar, which is exactly why this hypothesis's block boundary MUST be derived from an absolute UTC timestamp rather than from a count of bars or of received signals — a bar-indexed constant would mean something ~240x different live.

MUST default `signal_block_secs` to 0 via serde and in TradingConfig::default(), so a stored config or a hypothesis file lacking the field behaves exactly as today. The baseline run must remain byte-identical to a run of the unmodified code — verify this explicitly (hash or diff the three-capital reports before and after your change) and say so in your report before quoting any variant number.

MUST NOT change TradingEngine::allocation_delta_to_order, the allocation_threshold comparison at any call site, apply_zone, the rebalance_interval_secs spacing logic, the RiskManager call sequence, the exchange lot-size check, the fee logic, or the orders_below_min counting arm. In particular do NOT implement this by raising rebalance_interval_secs — that is a different mechanism which `rebalance-spacing-15m` already tested and which this hypothesis is specifically designed to separate itself from.

MUST pass `cargo test`, including the existing compute_btc_target_* tests in src/trading/engine.rs and the simulator tests in src/backtest/simulator.rs — update an expected value only where the new field legitimately changes it (do not weaken or delete a test just to make it pass).

A promoted change still becomes its own PR against dev (per the pipeline's step 6) and is never merged automatically — a human reviews it like any other algorithm hypothesis. Flag explicitly in the PR description that this diff changes when the allocation target is recomputed on the LIVE order-submission path, per the 'anything touching live trading behavior gets flagged explicitly' rule in docs/self-improvement-loop.md.
MUST NOT touch src/exchange/bitflyer/*, .github/workflows/*, or the bitFlyer REST/WS client.

paper_reference.title: Systematic Trend-Following with Adaptive Portfolio Construction: Enhancing Risk-Adjusted Alpha in Cryptocurrency Markets
paper_reference.key_claim: For a momentum/trend composite on crypto, the signal's sampling timeframe is itself the binding trade-off rather than the indicator parameters: 6-hour bars delivered Sharpe 2.41 at 142 trades/month while 1-hour bars delivered Sharpe 1.54 at 847 trades/month, with H1/H4 losing to turnover and whipsaw and H8/H12/D1 missing short-lived momentum.
paper_reference.pros: Same asset class, recent sample (in-sample 2021, out-of-sample Jan 2022 - Dec 2024), and it models costs (4bp taker, size-dependent slippage against 5-minute volume, funding). It is the paper that motivated yesterday's H6 test, and shirube's own measurement then reproduced its DIRECTION emphatically at the capitals where the lot floor is inert. This variant uses it as a dose-response prediction rather than as evidence: the paper says H1 should sit between shirube's 1-minute baseline and its H6 result, which is a falsifiable statement about shirube's own next data point.
paper_reference.cons: Do not trust the numbers. The instrument is 150+ Binance PERPETUAL SWAPS traded cross-sectionally with a 70/30 long/short split, monthly asset selection by prior-month Sharpe, and ATR trailing stops; shirube is a single-asset BTC/JPY SPOT allocator with no shorting, no selection and no stop, so the reported Sharpe is largely a diversification result that cannot transfer. Thresholds were grid-searched in-sample on 2021 and the Table-5 timeframe comparison is not itself presented out-of-sample, so the H6 optimum may be an artifact of that search — which is a direct reason to expect shirube's own optimum to sit elsewhere and to measure it rather than assume it. Its 4bp taker fee is under a third of shirube's 12.8bp effective rate at the promotion capital, which moves where any frequency optimum sits. And shirube's standing finding is that there is no measured gross alpha at zero fee, so a slower clock can at best move the result toward the static mix; yesterday's H6 did exactly that and still did not cross it. Promotion stays gated on shirube's own Sharpe/drawdown/trade-count rule over the holdout.
